head: Post_Employment_Non_Compete_Clause
desc: The judiciary has consistently held that post-employment non-compete clauses are unenforceable as they violate the fundamental right to livelihood.

head: Right_to_Livelihood
desc: The fundamental right to livelihood takes precedence over any commercial necessity or investment in human capital when assessing the validity of restrictive covenants.

head: Non_Compete_Enforceability
desc: The rules governing the enforceability of non-compete clauses in India differ categorically depending on whether the clause is in an employment contract or a shareholder agreement.

head: Non_Compete_Clauses
desc: Non-compete clauses in India are primarily governed by Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

head: Section_27_Indian_Contract_Act_1872
desc: Section 27 generally voids agreements that restrain any person from exercising any lawful profession, trade, or business.

head: Post_Termination_Non_Competes
desc: Post-termination non-competes are usually void unless they fall under specific exceptions such as the sale of goodwill.

head: Restrictions_During_Employment
desc: Restrictions during employment are typically enforceable due to an employee's inherent duty of fidelity to the employer.

head: Section_27_Indian_Contract_Act_1872
desc: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, renders every agreement in restraint of trade, including post-employment non-compete clauses, void to the extent of such restraint.

head: Post_Employment_Non_Compete_Agreements

head: Section_27_Indian_Contract_Act_1872
desc: The statutory mandate of Section 27 overrides any contractual terms that attempt to restrain an individual from exercising any lawful profession, trade, or business after employment ends.
